record.title_md: Do any three longest paths in a connected graph have a vertex in common?
record.subject: Graph Theory

dossier_meta.catalog_title: Do any three longest paths in a connected graph have a vertex in common?
dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture Do any three longest paths in a connected graph have a vertex in common?
dossier_meta.context_text: It is a well-known exercise that every two longest paths in a connected graph have a common vertex. Skupien [S] showed connected graphs where 7 longest paths do not share a common vertex.
dossier_meta.references_text:
- *[G] T. Gallai, Problem 6. In Theory of Graphs (Proc. Colloq., Tihany, 1966), 362 Academic Press, New York, 1968.
- Z. Skupień, Smallest sets of longest paths with empty intersection. Combin. Probab. Comput. 5 (1996), no. 4, 429–436.
